title: Eval Prioritizer: real-time weighting of golden prompts for cohort-specific canaries
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Our current canary and shadow pipelines treat all golden prompts in scorecards equally. This leads to noisy early signals for customers with skewed input distributions (e.g., long-form vs short-form, multi-lingual cohorts). We need an Eval Prioritizer service that assigns real-time weights to golden prompts per customer cohort and surfaces a compact, high-signal probe stream to canaries and A/B tests.

Goal: Reduce false positives and accelerate detection of regressions that matter to specific customer cohorts by: (1) prioritizing golden prompts that are representative of a cohort's real traffic, (2) amplifying early indicators for high-value customers, and (3) integrating weighted signals into automatic rollback decisions and canary dashboards.

Success metrics (primary):
- Decrease noisy rollback events by >= 40% during staged rollouts (measured across last 3 staged rollouts).
- Reduce mean time-to-detect cohort-specific regressions by 30% (median detection latency from first anomalous token to alert).
- No regression increase on global aggregate eval scorecards (<= 1% change).

Scope: Implementation of a lightweight prioritization service, schema changes for Scorecard ingestion, dashboard widgets, canary config knobs that accept weighted probe streams, and an integration into the existing rollback orchestrator to use weighted aggregated signals as inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Eval Prioritizer service deployed behind feature flag in staging
Scorecard ingestion accepts per-probe weight field and persists to timeseries store
Canary orchestration can consume a weighted probe topic and compute weighted mean delta over configurable window
Dashboard shows cohort selector, top-10 weighted prompts, and live weighted-regression metric
Automated rollbacks (canary) can be triggered on weighted-signal thresholds and log the rationale
E2E test harness with synthetic cohort traffic demonstrates reduced false positives vs baseline
implementation_plan: Design: finalise weighting heuristic and initial feature set (Priya + Data Science) — 1 week
Service: eval-prioritizer (Go) that subscribes to golden-sample catalog, produces 'weighted-probe' Kafka topic — 2 wks
Schema: update scorecard proto to include 'probe_weight' and 'cohort_id' — 2 days
Ingestion: update scorecard pipeline to persist weight and compute weighted aggregates in TSDB — 1 week
Orchestrator: extend canary runner to accept weighted-probe topic and compute weighted delta & p95 signals — 1 week
Console: dashboard widget for cohort view, top prompts, and a compare-to-baseline panel — 1 week
QA & Safety: run shadow traffic for 2 weeks then progressive canary (1% → 5% → 20%) with manual gates — 2 weeks
Docs + Runbook: update rollout and rollback playbooks with examples — 3 days
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Stage A: enable service in staging with synthetic cohort streams and verify weighted metrics match offline simulation. Stage B: shadow mode for 2 internal customers (no traffic steering), collect metric deltas for 10 days. Stage C: open canary to 1% production traffic for 48 hours; if no elevated weighted-signal rollback conditions, move to 5% for 72 hours, then 20% with continued monitoring. Final: full enablement with opt-out per-customer flag. All stages require a preflight check (TSDB health, kafka backlog < 1 hour).
monitoring_signals: probe_coverage_ratio (what fraction of cohort traffic matched golden prompts)
false_positive_rate_estimate (based on historical calibration per cohort)
rollback_criteria: Primary auto-rollback trigger: weighted_eval_delta_10m exceeds cohort-specific threshold for 3 consecutive windows AND absolute weighted probe sample >= min_samples_for_cohort. Secondary: multiple cohorts show correlated weighted deltas + increase in customer errors in the same window. All auto-rollbacks must create a rollback incident with attached weighted prompt list and top contributing prompts. Manual approval required for rollback if customer_impact == high.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting weights to short-lived traffic patterns → Mitigation: exponential smoothing with min-lifetime for weight changes
Risk: Increased complexity for small customers with few matched probes → Mitigation: fallback to global-weight baseline and mark cohort as 'low-sample'
Risk: Schema change causing older consumers to fail → Mitigation: backwards-compatible proto with default weight=1
Risk: Attack surface where customers craft prompts to influence weights → Mitigation: rate-limit weight updates and require authenticated owner changes for catalog updates
test_plan: Unit tests for weight calculation and smoothing logic
Integration test: end-to-end weighted probe ingestion → TSDB aggregation
Chaos test: simulate lag in weighted-probe topic and validate canary backoff behavior
E2E: compare baseline vs weighted-prioritizer on historical rollout traces and measure false-positive reduction
notes: Data Science to provide initial weight priors (feature engineering: token-length, language, schema-match, historical error-rate).
This ticket intentionally focuses on 'prioritization' not on re-labeling golden prompts. Re-labelling workflows exist as separate PM work.
We will reuse existing canary rollback incident format; ensure extension for attaching 'weight provenance' metadata.
